A recent social media post claims that Vice President Kamala Harris stated, "those infected with COVID-19 who have recently been hospitalized, as well as those who have died, have all been vaccinated." This assertion has garnered attention and prompted questions about its accuracy. To provide clarity, it is necessary to analyze both the substance of the Vice President’s statements and the broader context surrounding COVID-19 vaccinations, hospitalizations, and fatalities.

First, it is important to establish whether Vice President Harris made such a statement. Public remarks and interviews given by Harris on the topic of COVID-19 vaccinations have consistently encouraged Americans to get vaccinated and have highlighted the effectiveness of vaccines in reducing the severity of illness. There is no record of her stating that all recent COVID-19 hospitalizations and deaths have occurred among vaccinated individuals. On the contrary, her statements have generally emphasized that unvaccinated people remain at higher risk for severe outcomes.

The claim itself also warrants scrutiny. Throughout the pandemic, data collected by health agencies have shown that vaccination significantly reduces the risk of severe COVID-19 illness, hospitalization, and death. While breakthrough infections do occur—meaning vaccinated individuals can still contract COVID-19—the proportion of severe cases and fatalities among vaccinated populations has been markedly lower, particularly prior to the availability of updated booster shots and the emergence of new variants.

During surges associated with newer variants or periods when vaccine-induced immunity wanes, there have been increases in cases among vaccinated individuals, especially those with underlying health conditions or the elderly. However, the majority of severe hospitalizations and deaths have been consistently found among the unvaccinated, especially in the earlier stages of mass vaccination campaigns. More recent data from health authorities indicate that as overall vaccination rates increase, the absolute number of hospitalizations among vaccinated individuals may rise, but this is largely a reflection of the high proportion of the population that is vaccinated. Crucially, rates of severe outcomes remain higher among the unvaccinated.

The suggestion that "all" recent COVID-19 hospitalizations and deaths are among the vaccinated is not supported by available data. While breakthrough hospitalizations and deaths do occur, they do not account for the entirety of cases, and reports from hospitals and public health officials continue to cite unvaccinated individuals as those at greatest risk for severe disease. The core claim of the social media post is therefore inaccurate and misrepresents both the content of Kamala Harris’s public statements and the actual distribution of COVID-19 hospitalizations and deaths by vaccination status.

In summary, there is no evidence that Vice President Kamala Harris stated all recent hospitalizations and deaths due to COVID-19 have occurred among the vaccinated. Public health data show that the risks remain highest for the unvaccinated, though breakthrough cases do occur. Fact-checking the post reveals that it mischaracterizes both Harris’s stance and the epidemiological reality, potentially contributing to misinformation about vaccine effectiveness and public health outcomes.

Mặc dù có những trường hợp nhiễm trùng đột phá - tức là những người đã tiêm chủng vẫn có thể bị nhiễm virus - nhưng tỷ lệ cao hơn trong số các trường hợp nặng và tử vong ở nhóm đã tiêm chủng vẫn thấp hơn đáng kể, đặc biệt trước khi các mũi tiêm nhắc lại cập nhật được triển khai và sự xuất hiện của các biến thể mới.

Trong các đợt bùng phát liên quan đến các biến thể mới hoặc giai đoạn mà miễn dịch do vaccine suy giảm, đã có sự gia tăng các ca nhiễm ở những người đã tiêm chủng, đặc biệt là ở những người có bệnh lý nền hoặc người cao tuổi. Tuy nhiên, phần lớn các trường hợp nhập viện và tử vong nghiêm trọng vẫn được ghi nhận là ở những người chưa tiêm chủng, đặc biệt trong giai đoạn đầu của chiến dịch tiêm chủng đại trà. Các dữ liệu gần đây từ các cơ quan y tế cho thấy rằng khi tỷ lệ tiêm chủng tổng thể tăng lên, số ca nhập viện ở nhóm đã tiêm chủng có thể tăng, nhưng điều này chủ yếu phản ánh tỷ lệ cao của dân số đã tiêm chủng. Quan trọng hơn, tỷ lệ các kết quả nghiêm trọng vẫn cao hơn ở nhóm chưa tiêm chủng.

Khẳng định rằng "tất cả" các ca nhập viện và tử vong gần đây do SARS-CoV-2 đều xảy ra ở những người đã tiêm chủng không được hỗ trợ bởi các dữ liệu hiện có. Mặc dù có các ca nhập viện và tử vong đột phá, nhưng chúng không chiếm phần lớn các trường hợp, và các báo cáo từ bệnh viện và các quan chức y tế công cộng vẫn chỉ ra rằng những người chưa tiêm chủng là nhóm có nguy cơ cao nhất đối với bệnh nặng. Do đó, nội dung bài đăng trên mạng xã hội là không chính xác và đã làm sai lệch cả nội dung các phát biểu công khai của Kamala Harris cũng như sự phân bố thực tế các ca nhập viện và tử vong theo tình trạng tiêm chủng.

Tóm lại, không có bằng chứng cho thấy Phó Tổng thống Kamala Harris từng nói rằng tất cả các ca nhập viện và tử vong gần đây do SARS-CoV-2 đều xảy ra ở những người đã tiêm chủng. Dữ liệu y tế công cộng cho thấy nguy cơ vẫn cao nhất ở những người chưa tiêm chủng, mặc dù vẫn có các ca nhiễm đột phá. Việc kiểm chứng bài đăng cho thấy nó đã sai lệch cả lập trường của Harris và thực tế dịch tễ học, có thể góp phần vào thông tin sai lệch về hiệu quả của vaccine và các kết quả y tế công cộng.

A recent social media post claims that actor Jim Carrey stated, “the coronavirus has proven that it is easier to manipulate the whole world through fear if you control the mass media, scientific and medical sectors.” This statement has been widely circulated online, leading to questions about its authenticity and the context in which it may have been made. Here, we examine the origins of this claim, provide background on Jim Carrey’s public statements, and analyze the accuracy of the attribution.

Jim Carrey is a well-known actor and comedian, recognized for his roles in films such as "The Mask," "Liar Liar," and "Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind." In recent years, Carrey has also gained attention for his political activism and outspoken commentary on social and political issues, particularly on his social media platforms. However, Carrey’s public statements have primarily focused on issues such as political leadership, environmental concerns, and mental health awareness. While he has occasionally commented on media influence and disinformation, there is no verifiable record of him making the specific statement attributed to him in the viral post.

A thorough review of Jim Carrey’s verified social media accounts, interviews, and public appearances reveals no evidence that he said the coronavirus was proof that the world could be manipulated through fear by those controlling the media, scientific, or medical sectors. No reputable news outlets or transcripts from interviews contain this quote or any paraphrase of this sentiment attributed directly to Carrey. Furthermore, Carrey has not been publicly associated with COVID-19 conspiracy theories or statements undermining scientific or medical authorities during the pandemic.

It is important to note that during the COVID-19 pandemic, misinformation and misattributed quotes have proliferated online. High-profile celebrities are often targets of such misinformation because their names carry significant influence, potentially lending false credibility to controversial views. The quote in question closely mirrors common conspiracy narratives that emerged during the pandemic, suggesting that the public was manipulated by coordinated efforts involving the media and scientific community. However, attributing these views to Jim Carrey without substantiation misleads the public and distorts the record of his actual statements.

In conclusion, the claim that Jim Carrey said the coronavirus demonstrated the ease of manipulating the world through fear by controlling the mass media and scientific sectors is not supported by any credible evidence. The quote does not appear in any verified records of Carrey’s public statements, and there is no indication that he has expressed this perspective. As with all viral claims, especially those involving celebrities and sensitive topics like the COVID-19 pandemic, it is essential to verify the authenticity and context of attributed statements before sharing them further.

A claim circulating on social media alleges that Dalila Jakupović, a Slovenian tennis player, became ill at the Australian Open as a result of receiving the COVID-19 vaccination. This post suggests a direct link between her health incident on the tennis court and the COVID-19 vaccine. To assess the veracity of this claim, it is important to examine the events in question, the timeline, and available information about Jakupović’s health and the circumstances of her illness.

Dalila Jakupović is a professional tennis player from Slovenia who participated in the Australian Open qualifying rounds in January 2020. During her match, Jakupović experienced severe breathing difficulties and was forced to retire from her game. The incident was widely reported at the time, including coverage by major international news outlets. Witnesses noted that Jakupović collapsed to her knees and had to be assisted off the court. She later spoke to the media, describing the episode as frightening and attributing her breathing issues to the poor air quality caused by bushfire smoke that was affecting Melbourne during the 2020 Australian Open.

At the time of the Australian Open qualifying matches in January 2020, Australia was experiencing some of the worst bushfires in its history. The fires produced hazardous levels of smoke pollution in Melbourne, leading to widespread health warnings and concerns about the safety of outdoor events. Tennis players and other athletes expressed alarm about being asked to compete in such conditions, and the tournament organizers faced scrutiny over their decision to proceed with matches despite the air quality warnings.

It is important to note that the COVID-19 pandemic was not yet a global public health emergency in January 2020, and COVID-19 vaccines were not available at that time. The first COVID-19 vaccines were developed and authorized for emergency use much later in 2020, with the initial global vaccine rollouts occurring in December 2020 and early 2021. Therefore, it would have been impossible for Jakupović or any other tennis player to have received a COVID-19 vaccination prior to or during the January 2020 Australian Open qualifying tournament.

Moreover, Jakupović herself has publicly stated that her breathing difficulties were brought on by the smoke from the bushfires, not by any vaccination or illness related to COVID-19. There are no credible reports or evidence linking her illness to vaccination, and the timeline makes such a connection implausible.

In summary, the claim that Dalila Jakupović became ill at the Australian Open due to the COVID-19 vaccination is false. The incident occurred before COVID-19 vaccines were available, and the cause of her illness was widely attributed to bushfire smoke inhalation. Misinformation linking her health episode to COVID-19 vaccination is not supported by facts or the timeline of events.

Palot aiheuttivat haitallista saviilmanlaatua Melbournessa, mikä johti laajasti levitettyihin terveysvaroituksiin ja huoliin ulkoisten tapahtumien turvallisuudesta. Tennisilimestyt ja muut urheilijat ilmaisivat huolta siitä, että heidän oli pakko kilpailla näissä olosuhteissa, ja turnausjärjestäjät kohtasivat tarkastelua heidän päätöksestään jatkaa otteluita ilmanlaadun varoituksien vuoksi.

On tärkeää korostaa, että koronaviruspandemia ei ollut vielä maailmanlaajuisena julkishälvityksenä tammikuussa 2020, ja koronavirusvaccineja ei ollut tuolloin saatavilla. Ensimmäiset koronavirusvaccineet kehitettiin ja hyväksyttiin hätäkäytössä myöhemmin vuonna 2020, ja ensimmäiset globaaliset vaccinointikampanjat alkivat joulukuussa 2020 ja tammikuussa 2021. Siksi Jakupovićille tai mille tahansa muulle tennisilimestykselle ei olisi ollut mahdollista saada koronavirusvaccinointia ennen tai aikana tammikuussa 2020 olevaa Australian avoinna turnauksen kvalifikaatio-ottelua.

Ei ole uskottavia raportteja tai tietoa, joka liittää hänen sairaudensa vaccinointiin, ja ajankäytön perusteella tällainen yhteys on mahdoton.

Yhteenvetona väite siitä, että Dalila Jakupović sairastui Australian avoinna turnauksessa koronavirusvaccinoinnin vuoksi, on väärä. Tapahtuma tapahtui ennen kuin koronavirusvaccineja oli saatavilla, ja hänen sairaudensa syy oli laajasti liitetty metsäpalojen saviin. Väärinlajiin perustuva yhteys hänen terveysongelmaansa koronavirusvaccinointiin ei ole perustettu faktoihin tai ajankäytön perusteella.
